newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker rates steady, activity good.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker rates steady, activity good.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the Middle East Gulf was good on Friday, with rates steady and showing some signs of slight improvement, shipbrokers said.
By mid-afternoon one ULCC and two VLCCs had been seen-- Vela chartered the 350,000 tonner Tina, heading for the Red Sea, while the VLCCs were Japan and Singapore bound.
Brokers said VLCC trips to the East remained at W50.75, while vessels bound for Japan settled at last done levels of W56. Western voyages were seen to command around W50.
"It is anticipated that around 70 vessels will be available within the next four weeks, and owners are looking to build upon this week's gains, however slight," a London broker said.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med rose to W100, up W5 from Thursday's levels.
In the inter-UKC sector, rates picked up to W97.5, though as low as W95 was seen.
"There has been a slight decrease in vessel availability which has led to this increase," a broker said.
Caribbean tankers saw rates for 70,000 tonners making upcoast-U.S trips fall to W142.5 as evidenced by Exxon's chartering of the Bona Spring.
The West African market wallowed in a dearth of fixtures, with rates remaining at W62.5 for 260,000 tonners and W82.5 for 130,000 tonners to the U.S. By mid-afternoon no vessels had been seen.
